sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.detail: committed first — timestamp above, before any market number
sections.markdown:
**Archetype changed to `holdco_discount_narrowing`** (from sourcing's suggested `derated_compounder_rerating`): a "de-rated, re-rating" premise requires knowing a multiple compressed — unverifiable under the Phase-1 price ban. Sony instead offers a dated, filing-confirmed SOTP catalyst chain: the Oct 1, 2025 partial spin-off of Sony Financial Group (SFGI) to ~16.4% equity-method (a textbook "breakup"), plus an executed ¥500.0bn buyback (May 2025–Mar 2026) and a fresh ¥500bn/230m-share buyback authorized 2026-05-11→2027-05-10 — exactly the named-catalyst bar this card requires, argued on segment economics, not price.

### Earnings Quality Gate (EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS, run before estimates committed)
- **Accruals ratio:** FYE-Mar-2026 continuing-ops net income attributable ¥1,030,893mn vs continuing-ops operating cash flow ≈¥1,945,617mn → (NI−CFO)/total assets (¥15,683.5bn, FYE-Mar-2026) ≈ **−5.8%** [Sony 6-K, FY ended March 31, 2026 results]. Negative — cash generation exceeds reported earnings, the opposite of the ">10% = earnings outrunning cash" flag. Could not build a clean 3-year trend: the Oct-2025 SFGI spin-off deconsolidated a large balance-sheet block, so average-total-assets is not cleanly comparable YoY — flagged rather than smoothed over.
- **Cash-conversion trend:** consolidated operating income grew +13.4% YoY (record) while operating cash flow was reported "essentially flat YoY" (≈¥1,966.3bn vs ≈¥1,945.6bn across two summaries of the same release). Margin expansion outrunning cash conversion is an explicit gate divergence flag — **OPTICS-class**, not manipulation-class: plausible benign drivers are working-capital build behind I&SS's +20.2% volume growth and the ≈¥208bn of restructuring/impairment charges (Bungie ¥120.1bn, Sony Honda Mobility EV exit ¥44.9bn, Pixomondo ¥27.1bn, display assets ¥16.5bn, Semiconductor Israel ¥19.9bn) landing P&L-side in the same period as related cash outflows. **Haircut applied:** I&SS and Music segment OI growth rates used below are shaded ~2pp below the raw reported YoY prints pending Phase 2 review of the actual cash-flow note.
- **Related-party gravity:** SFGI is now a ~16.4% equity-method associate (from wholly-owned) post the Oct 1, 2025 spin-off — any continuing commercial ties between Sony's consumer/media businesses and its former financial arm need a related-party check in Phase 2; % of revenue not found in sources reviewed. The Sony–TSMC image-sensor JV is a non-binding MOU only — no related-party transactions exist yet to assess.
- **Structure flags:** none confirmed beyond the two above (checked: capitalized content/software-development-cost risk-factor language is qualitative only, no creeping-capitalization figure disclosed in sections reached; segment receivables/inventory detail not located in the excerpts obtained — flagged as unreviewed, not asserted clean).
- **Action rule:** no manipulation-class flag confirmed → proceed. One optics-class flag (margin/cash-conversion divergence) → haircut applied above and logged for the Phase-2 pre-mortem.

### Segment structure note
Financial Services is **excluded from the forward build**: ~80%+ of SFGI was distributed to Sony shareholders in kind on Oct 1, 2025 and Sony retains only ~16.4%, equity-method, immaterial to consolidated economics going forward [Sony 6-K, Sept 2025 spin-off scheme]. The five continuing operating segments are Game & Network Services (G&NS), Music, Pictures, Entertainment Technology & Services (ET&S), and Imaging & Sensing Solutions (I&SS).

### Per-segment SOTP build, FYE March 31, 2026 (all figures cited to Sony's FY-ended-March-2026 results release / 20-F unless marked ANALYST EST.)

**I&SS (image sensors/semiconductors):** Sales ¥2,059.0bn (+20.2% YoY), OI ¥357.3bn (+36.8% YoY, 17.4% margin); segment capex ¥265.3bn, of which ¥246.7bn for image-sensor capacity. Reinvestment rate (capex/OI, ANALYST-COMPUTED proxy) ≈74%; ROIIC proxy (ΔOI ¥96.1bn / prior-period capex, ANALYST EST.) ≈30-36%. g = reinvestment × ROIIC ≈22-27%, but I dial the DCF to a steadier 15% (yrs 1-3) fading thereafter rather than extrapolate one blow-out year. **Moat:** image-sensor technology/scale (Sony's own risk factors claim only "a strong competitive advantage," no house share % — the ~50% global CMOS share figure circulating is trade-press, not filing-cited, so it is NOT a load-bearing citation here). Moat-widening evidence: ¥246.7bn capacity capex + non-binding TSMC JV MOU toward a "fab-lite" model. **Fade risk named explicitly:** Feb-2026 trade press reports Apple diversifying sensor sourcing toward Samsung — a real customer-concentration/dual-sourcing risk; fade year set at **7**, not the default 10, given this.

**Music:** Sales ¥2,090.5bn (+14.8%), OI ¥447.0bn (+25.1%, 21.4% margin — highest of any segment). Reinvestment is catalog/artist-advance-led, not PP&E capex; no segment capex figure was locatable in the sources reached, so reinvestment rate is qualitative-only: **low** (asset-light), ROIIC qualitative: **high** (streaming +9% recorded music / +14% publishing revenue growth converting near 1:1 into OI given fixed catalog cost base). **Moat:** catalog scarcity + label consolidation; fade year **10** (durable, scarcity-based).

**G&NS:** Sales ¥4,570.1bn (+0.6%), OI ¥463.3bn (+10.4%, 10.1% margin); monthly active users hit a record 125 million in the March quarter. Reinvestment: platform/content R&D, no segment capex cited; consolidated R&D was ¥762.0bn (6.1% of sales, +¥27.4bn YoY) — largely G&NS+I&SS but not split by segment in sources reached. **Moat:** installed-base network effects; fade year **10**, tempered by console-cycle timing risk (not modeled as a discrete kill event here — that is Phase 2's job).

**Pictures / ET&S:** Pictures OI ¥104.9bn (-10.6%, 7.1% margin) — no durable moat named, treated as a going-concern annuity at modest growth. ET&S OI ¥158.6bn (-16.9%, declining on display-category weakness) — no moat, fade immediate to WACC, near-zero excess-return contribution to SOTP value.

### Discount rate, terminal value, multiple-survival test
COE/WACC used: **8.5%** (within the 8-10% house band; low end argued on globally diversified cash flows + moat quality in the two largest-value segments). Terminal g: **3.2%** (blended long-run nominal GDP across Sony's globally diversified revenue geography — US/EU/Japan/EM mix). Fade to WACC by the segment-specific years above (I&SS 7, Music/G&NS 10, Pictures/ET&S immediate). **Multiple-survival test (derived, not observed):** at terminal state ROIIC fades to WACC, so g = reinvestment-rate × WACC ⇒ reinvestment rate = g/WACC, and implied terminal EV/EBIT = (1−g/WACC)/(WACC−g) = **1/WACC ≈ 11.8x** — derived from my own WACC/g assumptions, not observed from Sony's actual traded multiple. Phase 2 must compare 11.8x against the real entry multiple; if entry already sits above ~12x EV/EBIT, this is multiple expansion wearing a DCF costume and must say so.

### Owner-earnings bridge (from reported NI, continuing operations, FYE Mar-2026)
NI attributable ¥1,030,893mn → (+) D&A embedded in segment capex intensity (not separately segment-cited; consolidated capex ¥804.9bn vs ¥829.8bn prior year) → (−) growth capex, of which ¥265.3bn is I&SS capacity-specific and treated as growth, not maintenance, given the +20% volume growth funding it → (+) add back ≈¥208bn of one-off restructuring/impairment charges (Bungie, SHM EV exit, Pixomondo, display, Semiconductor Israel) as non-recurring → SBC undisclosed in sources reached; left as a data gap, not estimated, to avoid a fabricated figure. Dividends: ¥25/share paid this year (total ¥148.6bn, 47th consecutive year), guided to ¥35/share next year — net_div_yield_pct_pa left null per Phase-1 scope (requires a share price/market cap denominator, banned here). Buybacks: ¥500.0bn executed this year; ¥500bn/230m-share (3.89% of shares out) authorized 2026-05-11→2027-05-10 — a real, dated capital-return catalyst for the holdco-discount thesis.

### Sensitivity — the 2-3 load-bearing assumptions (>70% of SOTP value)
1. **I&SS OI durability/growth** (¥357.3bn OI, +36.8% YoY on ¥265.3bn cited capacity capex) — citation: Sony FYE-Mar-2026 results release, segment table. Swing: if the Apple/Samsung dual-sourcing risk crystallizes and growth reverts to high-single-digits, this segment's SOTP contribution roughly halves.
2. **Music OI durability** (¥447.0bn OI, +25.1% YoY, 21.4% margin) — same citation. Swing: streaming growth (+9%/+14% cited) decelerating to low-single-digits caps OI growth near-flat; scarcity-moat argument is the load-bearing defense.
3. **G&NS platform monetization** (¥463.3bn OI on 125m MAU record) — same citation. Swing: MAU growth stalling or a soft console-cycle transition compresses the largest-revenue segment's OI base the SOTP is built on.
Together these three equal ¥1,267.6bn of ¥1,447.5bn consolidated OI (≈87.6%) — before even weighting I&SS/Music higher in the SOTP than declining Pictures/ET&S — comfortably clearing the >70% bar.

sections.heading: Priors disclosure
sections.detail: one sentence, from memory, written before document work
sections.markdown: What I believe the market narrative is: before opening a single filing, my prior was that the market sees Sony as a conglomerate that has already completed its transformation into a content-and-recurring-revenue compounder, with PlayStation Network services and its market-leading image-sensor semiconductor business as the crown-jewel growth engines justifying a re-rating away from the old low-multiple electronics-conglomerate discount, and the Music/Pictures IP library plus the Financial Services separation seen as further sum-of-the-parts value unlocks.

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** Sony has completed its transformation into a content-and-recurring-revenue compounder, with PlayStation platform economics, music catalog scarcity, and a leading image-sensor position justifying a premium multiple. The SFGI spin-off simplified the structure, and the ongoing buyback signals management confidence in undervaluation.
**Why wrong:** The spin-off extracted the easy discount. What remains is governance-structural — cross-subsidization across segments, conglomerate overhead, and no pressure to break up further. Markets price buybacks at announcement, not at completion — the ¥500bn authorization is already in the price. Without a forward catalyst to unlock residual value, the discount can persist indefinitely. G&NS underlying OI is flat (the ¥57.2bn FX/impairment comparison padding masks this). I&SS faces discrete socket-loss risk, not a smooth fade.
**What proves us wrong:** (1) No further restructuring, spin-off, or activist pressure announced within 12 months — discount persists or widens. (2) Apple formally dual-sources image sensors, hitting I&SS revenue >15%. (3) G&NS OI declines as the FX tailwind and Bungie-impairment comparison benefits reverse in FYE-Mar-2027.

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts
sections.detail: >=3, observable, current, each citing a dossier/filing line
sections.markdown:
1. **G&NS OI padded by non-operational items** — Sony FYE-Mar-2026 results release, segment note: G&NS operating income includes a ¥32.7bn foreign-exchange benefit (favored USD/JPY rates) and a ¥24.5bn favorable comparison from the prior-year Bungie impairment charge. Together these represent ~12% of reported G&NS segment OI (¥463.3bn). Excluding both, underlying G&NS OI growth is approximately flat YoY, removing the growth narrative from the thesis's largest revenue segment.
2. **SFGI spin-off discount already realized** — The Oct 1, 2025 partial spin-off of Sony Financial Group distributed ~80% of SFGI to shareholders in kind. Any holdco-discount narrowing from financial-services separation has already been recognized by the market in the 9+ months since completion. The residual discount is structural (governance, cross-subsidization, conglomerate overhead), not event-driven — and the thesis names no catalyst that would close the structural component.
3. **I&SS customer-concentration is binary, not a fade** — Sony's own FYE-Mar-2026 risk factors disclose that "a limited number of customers" account for a "significant portion" of image sensor sales. The Feb-2026 trade press reports of Apple diversifying toward Samsung sensor sourcing compound this: losing one major smartphone socket is a discrete ~20%+ segment-revenue event, not a smooth 7-year fade. The thesis's fade-year adjustment from 10 to 7 understates the downside tail.

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: It is [horizon end] and this position lost 30%. The most likely reason is the residual holdco discount widened rather than narrowed — the SFGI spin-off was the only structural catalyst the market rewarded, and without a follow-on breakup, buyback acceleration, or activist intervention, the discount reverted to or exceeded pre-spin-off levels. Simultaneously, I&SS lost a major smartphone image-sensor socket (Apple dual-sourcing materialized), cutting segment revenue ~20% and resetting the growth narrative that justified a premium segment multiple. G&NS OI flatlined as console-cycle fatigue set in and the ¥57.2bn of one-off FX/impairment-comparison benefits reversed, exposing the segment as a flat-revenue margin-harvesting business rather than a compounder. The market re-rated the conglomerate to the old electronics-conglomerate multiple — exactly the value-trap outcome the holdco_discount_narrowing base-rate notes warn against.

sections.heading: Bear attack
sections.markdown:
(Drew appends verbatim; survives the Judge verdict — never edited by a later stage)

**Drew (BEAR) — VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT, per 10-step protocol**

**1. Fact-check.** The SOTP computes nothing. Per-segment OI, WACC, and terminal g are cited, but no enterprise values, conglomerate value, or discount are calculated. You cannot narrow a discount you haven't quantified. The variant-perception block is blank. The pre-mortem is a one-line stub. These are not omissions — they are the thesis.

**2. Assumptions.** G&NS (47% of segment revenue, ¥4,570.1bn) grew sales +0.6% but OI +10.4% — margin harvesting on flat revenue, not compounding. Sony's filing discloses ¥32.7bn FX benefit and ¥24.5bn Bungie-comparison benefit inside G&NS OI (~12% of segment profit); underlying OI growth is near zero. I&SS +36.8% OI on a single year, with Apple/Samsung dual-sourcing flagged as a fade rather than a binary socket-loss event — lose Apple, lose 20%+ of segment revenue overnight.

**3. Variant perception.** Absent. A holdco-discount thesis must answer: why does the discount persist, and what closes it? Empty fields signal the analyst couldn't answer either question.

**4. Catalyst (Rule 3 violation).** SFGI spin-off (Oct 2025) and first ¥500bn buyback are past. The sole forward catalyst — ¥500bn buyback authorized 2026-05-11 — is already announced and running. Markets price buybacks on announcement, not completion. The catalyst_date "2027-05-10" is the buyback expiry, not an event. No forward catalyst exists.

**5. Base rate.** The 33% rate is generic. Discounts surviving a major partial spin-off are the stubborn ones — governance-structural (entrenched management, cross-subsidization), not event-driven. Post-spin-off residual-discount narrowing base rate is plausibly half.

**6. Sizing math.** None. No entry, target, or kill. A segment primer, not a position thesis.

**7. Disconfirming fact.** Sony FYE-Mar-2026 filing: G&NS OI contains ¥32.7bn FX tailwind and ¥24.5bn prior-year impairment comparison benefit. Excluding these non-operational items, underlying G&NS OI growth is roughly flat YoY, halving the thesis's largest value driver.

**8. Pre-mortem steelman.** SFGI spin-off extracted the available discount. Remaining 25-35% discount is governance-structural, persisting indefinitely. G&NS flatlines as efficiency exhausts; I&SS loses a smartphone socket. A "compounders-in-a-conglomerate" story becomes a value trap.

**9. Anti-gaming.** Archetype changed from `derated_compounder_rerating` pre-work — a card fit, not a finding. Multiple-survival defers entry-multiple check to Phase 2, immunizing the thesis against its own falsification condition during Phase 1.

**10. VERDICT: MAJOR_REVISION.** A segment primer, not a thesis. Required for survival: (a) SOTP with per-segment valuations, (b) quantified residual discount, (c) undisclosed forward catalyst, (d) variant perception. Absent these by next review, upgrade to KILL_RECOMMENDED.

sections.heading: Revision
sections.detail: analyst answers each numbered Bear point; may only lower estimates or widen down_pct without new evidence — raising p_up/up_pct/target requires a flagged "new evidence" citation
sections.markdown:
**Rough SOTP (first-pass; Phase-1 price ban prevents discount computation):**
- I&SS: ¥357.3bn OI, 0.70 tax-factor, fade yr 7, 15%→3.2% growth → ~11x → ~¥2.8tn
- Music: ¥447.0bn OI, 0.70 tax-factor, fade yr 10, asset-light → ~15x → ~¥4.7tn
- G&NS: ¥463.3bn less ¥57.2bn non-op = ¥406.1bn, 0.70 tax-factor, fade yr 10 → ~13x → ~¥3.7tn
- Pictures: ¥104.9bn, 0.70 tax-factor, no moat → ~9x → ~¥0.7tn
- ET&S: ¥158.6bn, 0.70 tax-factor, no moat → ~7x → ~¥0.8tn
- SOTP EV: ~¥12.7tn; +net cash ~¥1tn → **equity ~¥13.7tn**. Whether a discount exists or narrows is unknowable without market price.

**1. SOTP gap — CONCEDED.** I recited segment OI without multiplying to EV. The ballpark above remedies the blank. Without market price, I cannot defend the narrowing thesis.

**2. G&NS padding / I&SS binary risk — CONCEDED.** I flagged the ¥57.2bn non-op padding myself (disconfirming #1). Underlying G&NS OI ~¥406bn, flat YoY — a growth pillar removed. I&SS customer concentration is discrete socket-loss, not a smooth 7-year fade. I understated the downside tail.

**3. Variant perception — now filled above.** Market sees a post-restructuring compounder; I see structural discount with no forward catalyst to close it.

**4. Catalyst — CONCEDED.** SFGI spin-off closed Oct 2025. First buyback completed. Second buyback announced May 2026 — already priced at announcement. The 2027-05-10 date is an expiry, not an event. Rule 3 breached. No undisclosed forward catalyst exists.

**5. Base rate — CONCEDED.** Post-spin-off residual-discount narrowing is harder than generic 33%. p_up lowered to 0.20; down_pct widened to -30%.

**6-10.** Derivative. Archetype change was transparent (price-ban constraint) but deferring multiple-survival to Phase 2 is structurally protective — fair criticism. Pre-mortem now filled.

**Bottom line:** Without a forward catalyst, this is "the market will recognize hidden value" — explicitly not a thesis per the holdco_discount_narrowing base-rate notes. I cannot defend it. The Bear's MAJOR_REVISION is proportionate; absent new forward-catalyst discovery, this should go to KILL_RECOMMENDED.

sections.heading: Judge verdict
sections.markdown:
**Verdict: KILL — reason_tag: catalyst**

The thesis fails the cardinal requirement of the holdco_discount_narrowing archetype: a named, dated, forward-looking catalyst to close the discount. Both catalysts cited — SFGI partial spin-off (completed October 2025) and the first buyback — are rearview-mirror events. The sole remaining catalyst, a second ¥500bn buyback authorized May 2026, was priced at announcement. Markets do not reward buyback completion; the authorization date is the event, and it is behind us. The catalyst_date of 2027-05-10 is the buyback expiry, not a value-unlocking event. No forward catalyst exists, and the analyst concedes this without reservation.

The residual holdco discount — governance-structural, rooted in cross-subsidization and conglomerate overhead — has no mechanism to close inside the investment horizon. This is the classic pattern the base-rate notes warn against: "the market will recognize hidden value" is not a thesis.

The thesis was structurally incomplete at multiple levels: no SOTP computed in the original draft, kill criteria entirely blank, and variant perception initially absent. The rough SOTP in revision, while a good-faith repair, cannot be validated against market price under the Phase-1 price ban, leaving the discount itself unquantified and the narrowing premise untestable.

EV math is honest: p_up = 0.20 at +20%, p_down = 0.80 at -30%, expected_pct = -20%. G&NS underlying OI is flat once ¥57.2bn of non-operational FX and impairment-comparison padding is stripped out. I&SS customer-concentration risk is a discrete socket-loss event, not a smooth fade — the thesis's 7-year fade understates the downside tail.

Bear and analyst are in agreement. No salvage path exists. KILL.
